intro_html: One pot means one pot. The pasta cooks directly in the salsa and broth, which means the starch that normally goes down the drain stays in the pan and thickens the sauce for free. No colander, no second pot, no separate sauce. Each serving runs 584 calories with 31 grams of protein for about $2.26. Jarred salsa doing the job of six separate ingredients is one of the better shortcuts in a budget kitchen.
cost_closing_html: About $2.26 a serving. Salsa replaces canned tomatoes, chiles, onion, and half the seasoning at once, and pasta cooked in its own sauce means nothing gets poured away.
shop_smart: Jarred salsa is the workhorse here at nearly four cups. Buy the 16 oz jars on sale and check that tomatoes are the first ingredient rather than water or tomato puree.
Pasta shells cup the sauce better than any other cheap shape. Buy whichever store-brand box is lowest per ounce, since the shape matters more than the brand.
Build your own seasoning from chili powder, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, and onion powder. Every one of those is already in your rack and packets cost several times more.
Light sour cream stirred in at the end costs a fraction of what heavy cream does and gives you the same creamy finish with a little tang.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Heat the olive oil in your largest pot and brown the ground turkey hard, breaking it into crumbles and letting it stick a little before you scrape it up.
Add the diced onion and cook 5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, chili powder, ground cumin, dried oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and black pepper for one minute.
Pour in the salsa and the chicken broth, scraping the bottom of the pot clean, and bring it to a hard boil.
Stir in the dry pasta shells, making sure they are submerged, then drop to a simmer and cook uncovered 12 to 14 minutes.
Stir every few minutes so the shells do not weld to the bottom. This is the one part of a one-pot pasta that actually demands attention.
When the pasta is tender and the sauce has thickened around it, kill the heat and let the pot stand 5 minutes.
Stir in the light sour cream and the shredded cheddar off the heat so they melt smoothly instead of breaking.
portion_html: Weigh the pot, subtract the empty pot weight you wrote down, and divide by 14. One-pot pastas keep drinking sauce as they cool, so portion soon and let the scale keep the containers even. Each serving comes to 584 calories and 31 grams of protein.

head.description: One pot turkey Mexican pasta meal prep: shells simmered right in salsa and broth with ground turkey, finished with sour cream and cheddar. 584 calories, 31g protein, about $2.26 a serving.
head.keywords: one pot mexican pasta, turkey taco pasta, salsa pasta skillet, ground turkey pasta, budget meal prep, easy weeknight dinner
steps: Brown the ground turkey hard in olive oil in a large pot.
Add the onion, then the garlic, chili powder, cumin, oregano, garlic powder, onion powder, salt, and pepper.
Pour in the salsa and chicken broth and bring to a hard boil.
Stir in the dry pasta shells and simmer uncovered 12 to 14 minutes, stirring often.
Rest 5 minutes, stir in the sour cream and cheddar off the heat, and portion into 14 containers.
step_names: Cook the pasta in the sauce
